answers.answer: Shuffle all 4 Conflict III cards and place them at the bottom; shuffle 9 Conflict II and deal 5 on top; shuffle 3 Conflict I and deal 1 on top. The resulting 10-card deck is 1 I, 5 II, 4 III. Return all unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 2: ‘Result: a 10-card Conflict Deck — 1 Conflict I on top, 5 Conflict II below it, 4 Conflict III on the bottom.’

answers.answer: Both players start with two Agents on their Leader and a third Swordmaster Agent beside the board, three troops in their garrison and nine troops in supply, and 1 water. A four-player human starts at 1 VP; a three-player human starts at 0 VP.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 6: score ‘on the 1 space in a 4-player game, otherwise ... 0’; two Agents, third next to board, three cubes in garrison, nine in supply, take 1 water.

answers.answer: You may take a Reveal turn even with Agents left. Once you Reveal, you are skipped for the rest of Player Turns, so you cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards left in hand and revealed then; cards used on Agent turns do not provide their Reveal boxes. At Clean Up, all cards played on Agent turns and revealed cards go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘Agent turns are optional; you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents’; after Reveal, turns are skipped; only just-revealed cards’ Reveal boxes resolve; Clean Up moves all cards in front of you to discard.

answers.answer: Resources gained before placing your Agent, including from a legal Plot Intrigue, can pay the entry cost. Resources gained only after placement, from the destination or played Agent card, cannot pay for that entry. One card sends only one Agent, using one chosen Agent icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used for an Agent turn and may only be revealed.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: before placement resource gains can pay entry, but gains only after placement cannot; Agent Turn: ‘You choose only one Agent icon’; no-icon cards may only be revealed.

answers.answer: At a Combat space, you may deploy all three troops recruited this turn plus up to two more from your garrison, for at most five in this case. At a non-Combat space you cannot deploy recruited troops; they remain in your garrison. Troops are recruited from your supply into your garrison.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: cube recruits from supply to garrison; at a Combat space deploy any/all recruited this turn plus up to two from garrison.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to a space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; it does not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to bypass another player’s Agent at the destination, not your own Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy to draw a card, chosen immediately after placing your Agent and before resolving space or card effects. The same Spy cannot pay for both, though two different Spies can be recalled for the two different effects on one placement.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Spies: Spy Agent icon does not recall; Infiltrate bypasses another player only; Gather Intelligence timing is after placement, before effects; cannot recall same Spy for both.

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops contribute 4, one sandworm 3, and four revealed swords 4. If your final unit is removed, strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict you cannot participate in Combat Intrigue, which is available only to players with at least one unit there.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop 2, sandworm 3, sword 1; no unit means strength 0. Combat Intrigue: players with at least one unit in Conflict may play.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing earlier does not prevent playing later; the window closes after all players involved in Combat have passed consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply, not garrison, Combat markers reset to 0, and sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat: ‘You are not required to pass just because you passed earlier’; after all involved pass consecutively, resolve Combat; cleanup returns troops to supply and worms to bank.

answers.answer: With two tied for first in four-player play, each gets the second reward; the remaining players compete for the third reward, and nobody wins or takes the Conflict card. With the same tie in a three-player game, each tied player gets the second reward, no other reward is given, and nobody takes the card. A zero-strength player receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties table: exactly two tied first with 4 players means remaining compete for third; with 3 or fewer, no other rewards; nobody takes the card. Resolve Combat says 0 strength receives none.

answers.answer: Having one or more sandworms doubles your rewards once; two worms do not quadruple them. Control of a location and battle icons on Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For a reward allowing payment of 3 spice for 1 VP, you may pay again to receive the option a second time: 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 spice for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: ‘one or more’ doubles; control and battle icons excluded; optional reward cost may be paid a second time, with example 3 spice/1 VP or 6/2.

answers.answer: When you win a Conflict and take its card into your supply, check it against another face-up Conflict or Objective card there. Matching battle icons must be flipped face down as a pair for 1 VP. During Endgame, a wild icon can match any one of the three icons in your supply; flip the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: check when winning/taking Conflict card; face-up Conflict or Objective; ‘must’ flip; Endgame wild matches any of three.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP and lose it if you fall below 2; regain it upon reaching 2 again. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained after falling below 4 and earned again on returning to 4. The first player to 4 also takes the Alliance and its 1 VP, which belongs to the current holder. Tying the holder does not steal it; a challenger must rise above them, subject to the separate FAQ rule for a holder losing Influence.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory: 2 Influence VP reverses below 2; 4 track bonus retained; first to 4 gets Alliance and 1 VP; tying does not steal, rising above transfers.

answers.answer: Spend Persuasion during Reveal, before, between or after Reveal effects. You may pool sources to buy one card and split one source across cards. The Row is refilled to five immediately, so you may buy its replacement if you can afford it. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: Persuasion usable before/between/after Reveal effects, may pool or split, Row always five and replacement may be bought; acquired card goes face up into discard.

answers.answer: At each Maker space without an Agent, add 1 bank spice to its bonus spot; a visitor gains all accumulated bonus spice. Deep Desert and Hagga Basin offer base spice or, if you have Maker Hooks, their worm option; Hooks are required only when the effect specifies them and are retained, not spent. The Shield Wall prevents summoning to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery or Imperial Basin while present; removing it permits summoning at any Conflict. Sandworms are placed directly in your Conflict quadrant and never in a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers and Sandworms: unoccupied Maker gets bonus spice; visitor gains all; Hooks conditions and Wall restrictions; summoned worm goes to Conflict, never garrison.

answers.answer: At Recall, after the round, 10 or more VP by any player or an empty Conflict deck triggers Endgame. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then compare VP. Resource tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Phase 5 Recall triggers Endgame; Scoring says play Endgame Intrigue first, then most VP; tiebreakers list spice, Solari, water, garrison troops.

answers.answer: Set up 20 standard contracts by shuffling them, putting 2 face up on the board and 18 face down in the bank. Shuffle 4 additional Intrigues into the Intrigue deck and 4 additional Imperium cards into the Imperium deck. Shaddam is an optional Leader choice. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts stay in the box and are not part of standard CHOAM setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup: 20 contracts, two face up and remaining 18 face down; add four cards to each deck; Shaddam option; contrasting-back contracts are separate Rise of Ix set.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts, then replace it from the bank face up. If all contracts are taken, it instead gives 2 Solari. Harvest completes by sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining the printed spice amount during that turn in total, including other sources. Immediate completes as soon as taken. Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking/completing contracts: contract icon takes and replaces; if all taken reverts to 2 Solari; Harvest, Immediate, and Acquire card completion conditions listed.

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract for a board space after already sending your Agent there that turn, you must wait until a future turn because you must hold the contract when sending the Agent. On completion, announce it, gain its rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: CHOAM: ‘If you take a contract involving the board space where you've already sent your Agent this turn, you must wait until a future turn’; completion: announce, rewards, flip down, leave in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival. It takes the Ornithopter Objective. First Player goes to the human whose Objective shows that marker, and First Player alternates only between humans. Turn order is First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Setup: one shared scoring Rival; Rival gets Ornithopter Objective; First Player marker among humans; turn order listed; Rival never Reveals.

answers.answer: For an occupied indicated destination, ignore it and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try an empty post of the specified type, or ignore placement if none, then immediately reveal another card and continue the same Agent turn. Ignore ordinary space costs and effects; apply only revealed House Hagal effects. If the deck empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: ignore occupied destination and reveal again; Place Spy cards cause another reveal; ignore normal space costs/effects; reshuffle on empty or Reshuffle.

answers.answer: Shuffle the Objective deck after removing cards whose 1–3P or 4/6P marking does not match player count. Each human draws one at random and places it face up; the one with the First Player marker determines the first player. Shaddam may be used only with the CHOAM Module.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–5: do not use Shaddam unless CHOAM; remove nonmatching Objective cards, deal one per player; marker sets first player.

answers.answer: Solari, spice, water and sandworms are not limited; if the bank runs out, make any convenient substitution. If your personal troop supply is empty, you cannot recruit until troops return there. Resource gains come from the bank, and payments return Solari, spice or water to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: resources/sandworms ‘not meant to be limited’ and substitute if needed; gains from bank, payments returned; recruiting says no more troops until one returns to supply.

answers.answer: The phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict card, resolve the defensive troop bonus if applicable, then each player draws five cards. If Endgame does not trigger at Recall, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise and start the next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Player Reference list five phases; Round Start sequence reveals Conflict before drawing five; Phase 5 gives Recall and next-round steps.

answers.answer: Yes. After paying any entry cost and meeting requirements, the board-space effect, Agent-box effect and Faction Influence may be carried out in any order. But you must meet entry requirements before effects, so Influence gained from that visit cannot satisfy its own entry requirement.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs/meet requirements before effects; then space, card Agent box and Faction Influence ‘in any order.’

answers.answer: An optional arrow cost/effect can be paid and gained only once per turn, so you cannot repeat it in one Agent turn. Most card and space effects are mandatory; exceptions include ‘may,’ optional arrow costs, and the optional black-X trash icon. Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: Arrows: cost/effect once per turn. FAQ: most effects mandatory; exceptions include may, arrows, optional black-X; Intrigue conditions and costs must be met.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have none in supply, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect. If the placement effect specifies an Agent-icon type that must connect to the post, only a post connected to that specified icon is legal.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Spies: place on unoccupied post; if none in supply, may first recall one for no effect; some effects specify a required connected Agent icon.

answers.answer: No: Infiltrate bypasses only another player’s Agent, not your own. Recalling a Spy for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence still requires playing a card for an Agent turn. You cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement; two different Spies may be used for one Infiltrate and one Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Spies: Infiltrate cannot bypass your own Agent; FAQ says recall requires Agent-turn card; may recall two for different effects, never twice to Gather Intelligence.

answers.answer: The controller receives the separate control bonus whenever anyone, including themself, visits: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin. The Conflict winner for a critical location places their marker there, replacing any opponent’s marker. On revealing a Conflict for a space already controlled, its controller may deploy one troop from their supply directly to the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control: controller gets visit bonus; winner places/replaces Control marker; defensive troop comes from supply.

answers.answer: In a three-player tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; the Conflict winner retains first reward and card, with no further rewards. Tied for third receive nothing. If three players tie for first, each gets second reward; no other rewards and nobody wins/takes the Conflict card.
answers.evidence: Combat ties table: second-place tie gets third reward, winner keeps first/card; third tie gets nothing; three or more tied first in 4-player get second and no card/other rewards.

answers.answer: In a three-player Conflict with three distinct positive strengths, first and second receive their ordinary rewards; third receives nothing. The same applies in two-player play with a Rival: the Rival counts as a competitor, and ordinary third place gets nothing (third reward is used only for a tie for second).
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: with 2 or 3 players, ordinary first and second paid, ordinary third nothing; Rival is included in two-player count.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played during your Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues during Combat; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down, separate from your deck, and look at them any time; after resolving, put them face up in a discard pile by the Intrigue Deck. If that deck runs out, shuffle its discard into a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards section specifies timing, hidden storage and face-up discard; FAQ says exhausted Intrigue deck reshuffles discard.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard instruction discards a card of your choice from your hand, not an Intrigue unless specified. The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes an Intrigue of your choice from your hand. Secrets makes each opponent with 4 or more Intrigues give one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Discarding: from hand; not Intrigue unless specified. Intrigue section: separate trash-Intrigue icon; Secrets takes one random card from each opponent with 4+.

answers.answer: Trash effects can remove cards from your hand, discard pile or in play. Return ordinary trashed cards to the box and Reserve cards to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or the card directs you to trash itself. The Spice Must Flow’s acquire VP remains even if that card is later trashed.
answers.evidence: Trashing section lists eligible locations, destinations and optionality; FAQ says Spice Must Flow acquire VP is retained if trashed.

answers.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once at the moment the card is acquired. When you cannot draw because your deck is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing. Unused Persuasion is lost at the end of your Reveal turn and cannot carry over.
answers.evidence: Acquire box: one time at acquisition; acquiring cards says reshuffle discard when deck empty; Persuasion cannot be saved.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and cards revealed during Reveal remain face up and in play through the Reveal turn, so two Fremen Bond cards can activate one another regardless of order. They cease to be in play at Clean Up when all cards are moved to discard, unless trashed first.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond: all Agent and Reveal cards in play until Clean Up; two Bond cards activate one another regardless of order.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent just placed; it may be used on another Agent turn in the same round. Retreat moves a troop from the Conflict to your garrison. ‘Retreat any number’ can mean zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon and Retreat rules; FAQ explicitly says ‘Retreat any number’ allows zero.

answers.answer: A free-choice effect granting two Influence requires choosing one Faction; you cannot split it between two. A Faction-specific icon applies only to its named Faction. An Alliance icon requires holding that Faction’s Alliance token; a minimum-Influence effect requires meeting its stated threshold.
answers.evidence: Influence special rules: free-choice gain two cannot choose two different Factions; Alliance icon requires token; minimum Influence requirements are specified.

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied opponent takes the Alliance; if several were tied, the former holder chooses the recipient. If the holder falls to 3 or less and nobody has 4+, return the token to the board and the former holder loses its 1 VP.
answers.evidence: FAQ Alliance loss: formerly tied player takes token; if several tied former holder chooses; at 3 or lower with no 4+, return token; losing it loses VP.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used that turn. A card drawn after Reveal stays for next round, in addition to the normal five-card draw. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect stays face up until then, is used at that point, then discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ Draw timing: drawn during Reveal immediately reveal/use; after Reveal keep for next round then draw five extra; Plot with later Reveal effect remains until used then discarded.

answers.answer: No. A ‘when you win a Conflict’ Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first, because nobody wins. If you receive it as a reward for an outright win, you may play it immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ Combat and troops: win-trigger Intrigues cannot be played after tie for first; if received as winning reward they can be played immediately.

answers.answer: If VP and all four resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed track’s 12.
answers.evidence: FAQ Victory: all four resources tied, most recent Reveal turn wins; scores may exceed 12.

answers.answer: No. You must fulfill all contracts held for the same space with one Agent placement; completion cannot be delayed until after visiting. Contract completion is another effect of that Agent turn and can resolve in any order with space and Agent-box effects, but you must hold it when sending the Agent.
answers.evidence: FAQ Contract completion is mandatory: fulfill all same-space contracts with one Agent placement; resolves as another effect in any order; must hold it when sending Agent.

answers.answer: Shaddam does not start with the set-aside Sardaukar contracts; those are not initially in his possession. When acquiring a contract, his Sardaukar Commander ability allows choosing a set-aside Sardaukar contract instead of a generally available one. His Signet Ring deployment restriction begins immediately when playing Signet Ring to send an Agent and lasts for that turn only, not the round.
answers.evidence: FAQ Shaddam: may choose set-aside Sardaukar contract when acquiring; not stated as starting possession; deployment rule immediate on Signet Ring, lasts that turn.

answers.answer: Feyd’s token starts on the leftmost Training track space and remains on the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica begins with her Lady Jessica side face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Feyd token starts leftmost and stays at rightmost; Jessica starts Lady Jessica side; Reverend Mother Jessica may use ability on flip turn.

answers.answer: Moving from 1 to 3 counts as reaching 2; the ability can trigger again after losing Influence and later moving up to 2 again, but descending through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild’s Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: passing 2 while gaining counts, reaching again after loss/regain; only moving up counts. Guild’s Favor: Clean Up not a discard trigger.

answers.answer: Accept Contract is a Spice Trade icon: draw a card and, with CHOAM, take a contract; without CHOAM gain 2 Solari, also if none remain. Dutiful Service is an Emperor icon: gain 1 Emperor Influence and, with CHOAM, take a contract; without it gain 2 Solari, also if none remain. Accept Contract does not automatically advance Influence; Dutiful Service’s explicit Emperor Influence is its sole stated advance.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Accept Contract (Spice Trade), draw and contract/2 Solari; Dutiful Service (Emperor), 1 Emperor Influence and contract/2 Solari. Landsraad etc. not Factions; effects explicit.

answers.answer: Arrakeen is City, costs nothing, is Combat, and gives the visitor one troop recruited and one card drawn; its controller separately gains 1 Solari. Fremkit is Fremen, costs nothing, is Combat, and gives 1 Fremen Influence and a card draw. Research Station is City, costs 2 water, is Combat, and recruits two troops and draws two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table lists each icon, cost, Combat status and effects.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water; take all bonus spice and choose 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, summon two worms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water; take all bonus spice and choose 2 base spice or, with Hooks, summon one worm. The bonus spice is gained even when choosing worms. Hooks are not spent when summoning.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Deep Desert/Hagga Basin entries; Maker rules say visitor gains all bonus spice; Maker Hooks are retained, not spent.

answers.answer: Both options require City access and at least 2 Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. One option takes Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruits one troop and gains 1 water. The other gains 1 water and optionally removes the Shield Wall; it does not give a troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Sietch Tabr: both options, City and 2+ Fremen, no resource cost; only first recruits a troop.

answers.answer: Both visits cost 5 Solari and High Council is not a Combat space. First visit puts your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gives 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Subsequent visits give 2 spice, draw an Intrigue and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide High Council: 5 Solari each visit; first visit Councilor and ongoing 2 Persuasion each Reveal; subsequent visit effects; not marked Combat.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone gains one and 6 Solari once anyone has one. Each player may gain it only once. The new third Agent is available in the current round and for the rest of the game. A Rival gaining Swordmaster also reduces the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Swordmaster row lists costs, once per player, available this round and rest of game; Rival reduces human cost to 6.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege is a Landsraad space requiring 3 Solari and 2+ Emperor Influence. You may discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue; recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically grant Emperor Influence. It recalls another Agent, not the Agent just placed.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Privilege entry; Recall Agent rule says other Agent, not current one; not a Faction space and no Influence effect listed.

answers.answer: Shipping is a Spice Trade space requiring 2+ Guild Influence and costs 3 spice. It gives 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; the free-choice Influence need not be Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Shipping row: Spice Trade, 3 spice, 2+ Guild, 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any Faction.

answers.answer: Gather Support is Landsraad, not Combat: choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari; recruit two troops either way, and if paying 2 also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery is City and Combat: choose 0 or 1 spice; gain 2 Solari free or 4 Solari if paying 1 spice. Its controller separately gains 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide entries for Gather Support and Spice Refinery.

answers.answer: Heighliner (Spacing Guild, Combat) costs 5 spice, gives 1 Guild Influence and recruits five troops. Desert Tactics (Fremen, Combat) costs 1 water, gives 1 Fremen Influence, recruits one troop and optionally trashes a card. Sardaukar (Emperor, not Combat) costs 4 spice, gives 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue and recruits four troops. Only Heighliner and Desert Tactics allow normal deployment.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table lists costs/effects and marks Combat for Heighliner and Desert Tactics, not Sardaukar.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall is Landsraad with no cost: draw an Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if your Agent is there. Espionage is Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice, and gives 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, a card draw and Spy placement. Deliver Supplies is Spacing Guild with no cost and gives 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table entries for Assembly Hall, Espionage and Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent’s destination that turn; it can be played even without an enemy Spy connected there. Litany Against Fear’s red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ: False Orders movement and play condition; Litany red box timing.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If it remains unacquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ Manipulate: opponents cannot acquire; you may by other means without discount; otherwise remove end of next Reveal.

answers.answer: The Rival starts with four cubes at the bottom of Influence tracks; three troops in garrison and the rest in supply; two Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside the board; three Spies and 1 water in supply; score and Combat markers at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and retain the 2P Reshuffle card. The Rival is a scoring competitor: 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall and it can win.
answers.evidence: Rival setup lists components, 1 water, score/Combat at 0, and retaining 2P Reshuffle; Rival overview says it can win and 10+ VP triggers Endgame.

answers.answer: As soon as its total of Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water reaches its printed Swordmaster threshold, it spends that many resources and takes its third Agent, usable in the current round. If choosing resources, spend Solari first, then spice, Intrigue cards, then water; keep leftovers.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster: combined threshold, spending priority, leftovers, and current-round Agent.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, it spends each qualifying set: 7 Solari for 1 VP, 7 spice for 1 VP, 3 Intrigue cards for 1 VP, or 3 water for 1 VP. It cannot combine a mixed seven resources; only the specified same-resource sets count.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster: ‘whenever it has 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water, spend each such set for 1 VP.’

answers.answer: When choosing Influence, the Rival picks the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by leftmost priority icon. It gains and loses VP for reaching 2 and for Alliance possession like a human, but does not receive the 4-Influence track resource bonus. A numbered Hagal Influence icon refers to that position in its Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival rules: least Influence and priority tie break; Rival gets Influence VP/Alliances but not resource bonus; numbered icon refers to priority list.

answers.answer: No. For a two-destination Hagal card, use only the destination matching current conditions: Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping, or Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner. If the selected destination is occupied, reveal a new card rather than using the other destination.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: select only condition-matching destination; if occupied, reveal a new card without using the other destination.

answers.answer: Yes. At every Combat space, deploy up to two available garrison troops even if the card recruited none. Troops recruited at a noncombat space go into garrison. If a conditional 2+ Influence bonus is unmet, that bonus is simply omitted; it never prevents placing the Agent.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: Combat deploy up to two from garrison even if none recruited; recruited troops at noncombat go to garrison; lack of bonus never prevents placement.

answers.answer: For an unrestricted Spy, use the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing the third and final supply Spy immediately recalls the other two and triggers the printed Scheme. The Rival never recalls Spies to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes section states post choice, full-post behavior, third Spy Scheme, and no Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence.

answers.answer: If the Scheme recruits troops before Agent placement and that turn reaches a Combat space, deploy those troops too. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent; even if no legal post exists, ignore placement, reveal another Hagal card and continue the same Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes: Scheme troops deploy at Combat same turn; Place Spy with no empty specified post ignores placement and reveals another card.

answers.answer: The Rival collects all accumulated bonus spice at a Maker space. At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, with Hooks and a Conflict where worms are allowed, summon one or two worms respectively instead of base spice. If it summons none (no Hooks or protected Conflict), take base spice instead: 2 at Hagga or 4 at Deep Desert. Bonus spice is still collected; Imperial Basin always gives 1 base spice.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces: always collect bonus; worms at Hagga/Deep Desert with Hooks and permitted Conflict; if none, base spice; Imperial Basin 1.

answers.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal a Hagal card in turn order and add only its bottom swords to strength. If Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window, so they can respond afterward. A Rival without a deployed unit gets no bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat: beginning of Combat, at least one unit; add bottom swords only; reshuffle and repeat; humans then Combat Intrigue.

answers.answer: Yes: it receives control, defensive troop, battle-icon VP and sandworm-doubled Conflict rewards by normal rules. It always takes optional Conflict VP if it can pay or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward gives it 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat: normal control/battle-icon/reward rules, optional VP if payable; never takes contracts and receives 2 Solari.

answers.answer: During Resolve Reveal Effects, total Combat strength, announce it and set the marker at any point while resolving; update it as needed. Strength over 20 is marked by flipping to the +20 side and starting again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn and Strength: total/announce/set at any point while resolving, update as needed; over 20 flip marker to +20 and restart track.

answers.answer: A human Leader’s Signet Ring ability activates when Signet Ring is played on an Agent turn, not merely revealed. Card text may override usual game rules.
answers.evidence: Setup step 3: Signet Ring ability activates when played on an Agent turn, not revealed; Overview: cards of any type can override usual rules.

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon on a card returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for a powerful effect. This icon itself does not automatically mean Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate optional Spy recalls without a card for their stated effects.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts distinguishes Recall Spy icon from separate Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence recalls.

answers.answer: The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction means a card of your choice from your hand and cannot be an Intrigue unless specified; discard does not trash it.
answers.evidence: Trashing: separate icon trashes Intrigue from hand; Discarding: ordinary discard from hand, not Intrigue unless specified.

answers.answer: Yes. Sandworm doubling lets you take the one-Influence reward twice, choosing the same Faction or two different Factions. A single effect that says gain two Influence with free choice requires choosing one Faction for both; it cannot be split.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling example allows 2 Influence with same or two different Factions; Influence rule says a free-choice gain two cannot split.

answers.answer: Resolve the Rival’s printed Signet Ring ability on its Rival card when House Hagal shows that effect. It does not need a human Signet Ring card or a Reveal turn; the Rival follows its printed Signet Ring ability on its Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: follow Rival card’s printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities; Rival never Reveals. (Summary does not separately detail the specific Signet trigger.)

answers.answer: A Maker Hooks icon gives the Rival a token only if it lacks one; if it already has Hooks, it takes no second token. A Shield Wall removal effect removes the Wall only if the Rival has Hooks and the Wall remains. Without Hooks it is ignored; if the Wall is already gone it has no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons table lists outcomes for existing/missing Hooks and removed Wall.

answers.answer: Secrets is Bene Gesserit, has no entry cost and is not Combat. It gives 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws an Intrigue from the deck; each opponent with 4+ Intrigues then gives you one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Secrets row: Bene Gesserit, no cost, 1 Influence, draw Intrigue, opponent theft; it is not marked Combat.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin is Spice Trade, no entry cost, and is Combat. The visitor gains 1 base spice plus all bonus spice there. Its controller gets 1 spice; if visitor and controller are the same player, that player gets both effects, for 2 spice plus the bonus.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Basin (Spice Trade), Combat, no cost, 1 base plus bonus; controller gains 1 spice; controlled locations resolve both effects even for same player.

answers.answer: Reveal the new Conflict from the top of the deck and place it face up next to the deck, on top of any Conflict cards remaining from earlier rounds. Each player draws their five hand cards only after this reveal and any defensive troop bonus are resolved.
answers.evidence: Round Start: reveal Conflict and place it on top of any remaining previous rounds; defensive bonus then each player draws five cards.

answers.answer: Each player’s four Influence cubes start on the bottom spaces of the four Faction tracks. The four Alliance tokens start on marked areas of the four tracks; no human starts holding one. The Shield Wall token is placed on the marked area below Spice Refinery, so it is initially present.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 6: Alliance tokens on tracks, Shield Wall below Spice Refinery; each player places one cube on bottom of each Faction track.

answers.answer: In 3–4 player play, the First Player takes the first turn and play continues clockwise one turn at a time; a player who Reveals is skipped for the rest of the phase. Player Turns end once all players have Revealed. Combat Intrigue priority starts with First Player and continues clockwise. Each eligible player may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards or pass; passing is not binding, and the window closes after all involved players pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Player Turns and Combat sections specify clockwise order, skip after Reveal, phase end, First Player Combat priority, any number, and consecutive passes.

answers.answer: The three steps are Reveal Cards (reveal remaining hand), Resolve Reveal Effects (gain those cards’ Reveal boxes), and Clean Up (move cards in front of you to discard). Reveal effects may be resolved in any order; they need not follow card order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn lists the three steps and says Reveal effects resolve ‘in any order.’

answers.answer: Shuffle each human’s 10-card starter deck face down; shuffle Intrigue face down; without CHOAM omit marked cards, shuffle Imperium face down and deal five face up into the Row, with the rest face down; place Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow as separate Reserve stacks. The human Combat marker starts at 0. Spies, Councilor and Control markers start in the player’s supply; the Councilor goes onto High Council only upon the first visit, and Control markers are placed only when gaining location control.
answers.evidence: Initial card states and setup steps 4, 6: starter shuffled face down; deck/Row/Reserve preparation; Combat marker 0; remaining components including Spies in supply; Councilor/Control markers later placed by effects.

answers.answer: During a Reveal turn, ordinary Persuasion may acquire any of the five cards in the Imperium Row, or Prepare the Way or The Spice Must Flow from Reserve. Each card’s cost is shown at its top right. These purchases may be made during Reveal, before, between or after Reveal effects; ordinary Persuasion purchases are not made on Agent turns.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: during Reveal use Persuasion for Row or Reserve cards; cost at top right; spend before, between or after Reveal effects.

answers.answer: Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional; you may decline even if legal. A Shield Wall detonation icon lets you remove the token, so destruction is optional; once removed it is gone for the rest of the game and cannot return in a later round.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional; Shield Wall can be removed and is gone for rest of game.

answers.answer: The played card must have an Agent icon matching the destination, unless it has a Spy Agent icon and your Spy is at a connected observation post. Having a Spy connected to Shipping alone does not let a City-only card send an Agent there. With the Spy Agent icon, the connected Spy grants access to Shipping without being recalled.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn and Spy Agent icon: require matching normal icon or Spy Agent icon with connected Spy; connected Spy alone does not grant access to every card.

answers.answer: Yes. You may play a legal Plot Intrigue before placing the Agent, and resources it grants before entry are available to pay the cost. Resources from the Agent card’s Agent box or destination effects occur only after placement and cannot pay that same entry cost.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: on Agent turn play Plot Intrigue before placing; resources granted before entry join available supply; placement/card gains cannot pay same entry.

answers.answer: No. In two-player play, skip humans who have Revealed but continue the Rival’s Agent turns while it has an Agent in supply. Combat begins only once both humans have Revealed and the Rival has used all its Agents. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: two-player phase continues Rival turns after humans Reveal and proceeds to Combat after Rival uses all Agents; Rival never Reveals.

answers.answer: Standard board-space icon and Combat reference: Accept Contract—Spice Trade, no; Arrakeen—City, yes; Assembly Hall—Landsraad, no; Deep Desert—Spice Trade, yes; Deliver Supplies—Spacing Guild, no; Desert Tactics—Fremen, yes; Dutiful Service—Emperor, no; Espionage—Bene Gesserit, no; Fremkit—Fremen, yes; Gather Support—Landsraad, no; Hagga Basin—Spice Trade, yes; Heighliner—Spacing Guild, yes; High Council—Landsraad, no; Imperial Basin—Spice Trade, yes; Imperial Privilege—Landsraad, no; Research Station—City, yes; Sardaukar—Emperor, no; Secrets—Bene Gesserit, no; Shipping—Spice Trade, no; Sietch Tabr—City, yes; Spice Refinery—City, yes; Swordmaster—Landsraad, no.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table labels all 22 spaces’ Agent icons and marks Combat spaces.

answers.answer: When the Conflict card is revealed for a critical location you already control, you may deploy one troop from your supply directly to the Conflict without an Agent visit; this defensive bonus is optional (‘may’). After rewards, all Combat markers reset to 0 before Makers.
answers.evidence: Round Start defensive bonus: controller ‘may deploy’ a supply troop without Agent visit; Combat cleanup resets all Combat markers to 0.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you, then send one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied matching space; resolve the played card’s Agent box, not its Reveal box. You cannot reuse a card already in play or in discard, nor simply move an Agent already on the board; the turn calls for a card from hand and an Agent from your Leader.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: play one card from hand, send Agent from Leader to unoccupied space; use Agent box and ignore Reveal box.

answers.answer: The restriction applies immediately when Signet Ring is played to send the Agent, so Shaddam cannot delay it by resolving board-space effects first. It governs deployment on that turn.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications / FAQ Shaddam: restriction takes effect immediately on playing Signet Ring to send Agent; cannot postpone by ordering effects.

answers.answer: In four-player play with four different positive strengths, first, second and third receive their corresponding printed rewards. Fourth place receives none. The highest-strength player wins and takes the Conflict card, then checks for a battle-icon match.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: in four players ordinary first/second/third receive rewards; winner is highest and takes Conflict card; no fourth reward is described.

answers.answer: Players may choose Leaders or select them at random; random distribution is not required.
answers.evidence: Setup step 3: each player takes a Leader ‘(choose, or select at random).’

answers.answer: An ordinary draw comes from your own deck. If it is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing; you cannot choose a card directly from the discard pile.
answers.evidence: Drawing cards: ordinary draw from own deck; if empty shuffle discard into new deck; no direct discard choice stated.

answers.answer: Shuffle the House Hagal deck and place it near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card in the deck.
answers.evidence: Rival Setup: ‘Shuffle House Hagal and place the deck near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card.’

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human player. A token later acquired moves from the bank onto that player’s garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: all Maker Hooks in common bank; normal setup assigns none; later acquired token moves onto player’s garrison.

answers.answer: Yes. When a Combat Intrigue resolves and changes deployed units or otherwise alters strength, adjust the Combat marker during the Combat Intrigue window. Resolve rewards using the adjusted strength shown on the track after the window closes.
answers.evidence: Combat: if Combat Intrigue changes units/strength, adjust marker when card resolves during window; after consecutive passes, resolve using adjusted track strength.

answers.answer: Gained Solari, spice and water are taken from the bank. The summary does not permit taking resource tokens from another player’s supply; payments return resources to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: whenever you gain listed resources take from bank; whenever you pay return them to bank.
